title: Volume Bouldering
texts:
Using either set boulders in a commercial climbing gym or a training board with ample climbs (such as the Kilter, Moon, or Tension board), climb 20 problems in 1 hour that are about 1 or 2 grades below your flash grade.  For example, if you can flash v8 50% of the time on your chosen setting, then you would look to complete this workout using climbs that are v7 or v6.  Once you have completed a problem, rest for 2 minutes before moving on to the next climb.  

The goal of this workout is to focus on climbing each problem with optimal movement patterns. Since the problems will only be moderately difficult for you, avoid the temptation to “power through” moves and instead look for ways to conserve energy.

The problems can be a mix of climbs you have previously done or new climbs that you are looking to flash.  If you fall off a climb in the beginning, you can restart the problem again.  If you fall near the top of the climb, simply move on to the next climb.  If you begin failing on multiple problems or find that your technique is deteriorating, drop the difficulty of the problems.
